# Member Appeal — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date this letter is sent]

**To:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Morgan Foster
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-11**
- **Member:** Morgan Foster
- **Member ID:** W276906709
- **Reference number:** POC-EED29F7594-68772
- **Denied service:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
- **Plan:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield (Commercial/ACA), state of Kentucky
- **Governing policy:** Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1), effective 2025-11-15 — https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

---

## Why I am writing

I am appealing the denial of my partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which Anthem denied on 2026-08-11 under reference number POC-EED29F7594-68772. The notice states, in plain terms, that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure.

I am asking for reconsideration because the imaging in my chart appears to be exactly the kind of imaging the plan's own guideline asks for, and it describes exactly the kind of joint damage the guideline describes. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is needed. Below I have set the plan's published criteria side by side with what my records say, so a reviewer can compare them directly.

I am working from the portions of the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline that are available to me. The guideline lists further conditions that I have not reproduced here, and I respectfully ask Anthem to identify the specific criterion or criteria it applied in reaching this decision, so that I can respond to them directly.

---

## The plan's criteria, matched to my records

### 1. The type of imaging the policy asks for

The policy states:

> "Imaging reports obtained within the past 12 months describing the degree of cartilage damage as determined by either or both of the following methods: X-ray report or provider interpretation of x-rays that utilizes or can be correlated with the Kellgren-Lawrence grading system of osteoarthritis MRI report from a radiologist that utilizes or can be correlated with the modified Outerbridge or similar classification system related to articular cartilage injury and osteoarthritis"

My records: I had an MRI of the knee on **2026-06-27** — within twelve months of this request. It describes **full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition**, and grades my arthritis as **Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially**. That is an imaging study, obtained in the required timeframe, that describes the degree of cartilage damage and uses the Kellgren-Lawrence grading system the policy names.

### 2. The degree of joint destruction the policy describes

The policy states:

> "Imaging evidence of significant joint destruction and cartilage loss, defined as diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III – IV or Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 – 4, isolated to the medial or lateral knee compartment with no degenerative changes in the opposite compartment"

My records: my MRI reports **Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4** damage, located **in the medial compartment**, with **full-thickness cartilage loss and bone-on-bone apposition**. The grade documented in my chart is the highest grade named in this criterion, and it is described in a single compartment.

If Anthem's concern is the condition of the opposite compartment specifically, I would appreciate that being stated plainly, because my denial notice did not say so. I ask that the full MRI report be re-read on this point, and I am glad to have Dr. Lindqvist's office send the complete report and images again at no cost to the plan.

### 3. What the policy says an imaging report should describe

The policy states:

> "Imaging reports should be thorough and describe the presence or absence of subchondral cysts, subchondral sclerosis, periarticular osteophytes, joint subluxation, avascular necrosis, or bone on bone articulations. The degree of joint space narrowing should also be noted."

My records: the MRI expressly documents **bone-on-bone apposition** and **full-thickness cartilage loss** — the most advanced of the findings listed in this sentence. If the reviewer needs the report's description of the other features named above, that information is in the radiology report itself, and I ask that the complete report be obtained and reviewed rather than the summary alone.

The policy also states:

> "For x-ray interpretation, the provider shall submit a detailed imaging description that correlates with clinical findings of the requested procedure. In the absence of a detailed description, the provider may submit a report from an independent radiologist."

My records: the imaging in my chart is an MRI dated 2026-06-27, and its findings line up with my clinical picture — a positive provocative test on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain on examination.

### 4. Conservative treatment — completed, and then some

The policy states:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-surgical conservative management (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4)"

My records: I completed **16 weeks** of supervised physical therapy, from **2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17**, with **24 visits completed**, documented in my physical therapy discharge note. That is longer than the twelve weeks this criterion names. Separately, my imaging is graded **Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4**, which is the exception the plan itself wrote into this sentence.

The policy states:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

> "Physical therapy requirement includes ANY of the following: Physical therapy rendered by a qualified provider of physical therapy services Supervised home treatment program that includes ALL the following: Participation in a patient-specific or tailored program Initial active instruction by MD/DO/PT with redemonstration of patient ability to perform exercises Compliance (documented or by clinician attestation on follow-up evaluation)"

My records: my physical therapy was **supervised**, focused on **quadriceps strengthening and range of motion**, and is documented in a discharge note — physical therapy rendered by a qualified provider, the first option in the plan's list.

> "Complementary conservative treatment requirement includes ANY of the following: Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics 2 Adjunctive medications such as nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants 2 Intra-articular corticosteroid injection(s) 2 Alternative therapies such as activity modification, and/or a trial period of rest (e.g., from the aggravating/contributing factors), where applicable"

My records: I meet this more than once over. I took **NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief**, and I had a **corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-26 that gave only about two weeks of partial relief**. Anti-inflammatory medication and intra-articular corticosteroid injection are both on the plan's own list.

> "Failure of conservative management requires ALL the following: Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation More invasive forms of therapy are being considered"

My records: I finished a full course of therapy (16 weeks, 24 visits). My pain has been **progressive over 14 months and is unrelieved by rest**, and the injection relief lasted only two weeks. And a more invasive option is precisely what is now under consideration — the partial knee replacement Dr. Lindqvist has recommended and that Anthem has denied.

### 5. Documentation of duration, severity and function

The policy states:

> "Clinical notes describing symptom duration and severity, specific functional limitations related to symptoms, and type and duration of all therapeutic measures provided. If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented."

My records: **duration** — 14 months of progressive pain. **Functional limitations** — I **cannot climb stairs without assistance**, and I **wake 3 to 4 times a night** because of the pain. **Therapeutic measures and their duration** — 16 weeks and 24 visits of physical therapy with specific dates, 4 months of NSAIDs, and a dated corticosteroid injection.

The policy also states:

> "Reporting symptom severity – Severity of pain and its associated impact on activities of daily living (ADLs) and instrumental ADLs (IADLs) are key factors in determining the need for intervention. For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform ADLs and/or IADLs."

My records document the functional side of this directly: I am unable to climb stairs without assistance and my sleep is broken three to four times a night by pain. My most recent recorded pain score is **[pain rating out of 10 as documented in my chart — to be supplied from the office note dated [date]]**, and I ask that this be taken from my chart rather than assumed.

### 6. Reevaluation, knee stability, alignment and comorbidities

> "Clinical reevaluation – In most cases, reevaluation should include a physical examination. Direct contact by other methods, such as telephone communication or electronic messaging, may substitute for in-person evaluation when circumstances preclude an office visit. Clinical reevaluation must be done in reasonable proximity to the anticipated date of service such that the patient's condition would be unlikely to change by the date of service."

My records include a **physical examination** with **positive provocative testing on the affected side** and **range of motion limited by pain**. The date of that examination is **[date of my most recent office visit with Dr. Lindqvist]**, and if the plan needs a more recent reevaluation before the anticipated surgery date, Dr. Lindqvist's office can provide one.

> "Intact anterior cruciate ligament or documentation of stable knee examination (UKA may done with concurrent ACL reconstruction if all other criteria are met)"

This criterion is satisfied by either an intact ACL or a documented stable knee examination. The relevant finding is **[ACL status and/or knee stability exactly as documented in my MRI report and surgeon's exam note — to be supplied]**, and I ask that Anthem obtain it from the submitted MRI report and examination note.

> "Less than 10 degrees of fixed varus deformity for medial UKA"

> "Less than 15 degrees of fixed valgus deformity for lateral UKA"

My disease is in the **medial compartment**. The measured fixed deformity in my knee is **[fixed varus deformity in degrees as documented in my chart — to be supplied]**. I have not been told that alignment was the basis for this denial, and I ask that if it was, Anthem say so.

> "Where there are patient specific modifiable comorbidities that may adversely impact patient reported outcomes or the health status of the patient, a shared decision-making process to discuss these modifiable comorbidities with the patient is strongly recommended and should be documented."

My records show **no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker**.

---

## What I am asking for

I am asking Anthem to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-11 (reference POC-EED29F7594-68772) and to authorize the partial knee replacement, CPT 27446, as recommended by Dr. Lindqvist.

If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, I ask that Anthem:

1. Identify the **specific criterion** in Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1) that my imaging is said not to meet, and the specific finding in my MRI of 2026-06-27 that the reviewer relied on;
2. Confirm whether the **complete MRI report and images** from 2026-06-27 were in front of the reviewer, and obtain them if they were not;
3. Provide the **name, credentials and specialty** of the reviewer who made this determination; and
4. Advise me of my remaining appeal rights, including any external review available to me.

I am happy to have Dr. Lindqvist's office send any record, report, or image the plan needs, and to have my surgeon speak with the reviewer directly. Please contact me at [my phone number] or [my email address].

**Appeal timing and submission:** My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-07**. I am submitting this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also submit or check on my appeal at anthem.com, through the Sydney Health app, or by calling the number on the back of my ID card. My denial letter is the authoritative source for the address and deadline.

Thank you for taking a careful second look at this.

Sincerely,

**[Signature]**

Morgan Foster
Member ID: W276906709
[Date of birth]
[Mailing address]
[Phone number]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-11 (reference POC-EED29F7594-68772)
- MRI report dated 2026-06-27
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17, 24 visits)
- Office and operative planning notes from Dr. Lindqvist, orthopedic surgery
- Medication and injection records, including corticosteroid injection dated 2026-03-26
- [Any additional records my surgeon's office provides]
